newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan report on economy likely to be unchanged-EPA.
newsitem.headline: Japan report on economy likely to be unchanged-EPA.

text.p: The Japanese government's overall view of the economy will likely remain unchanged in a monthly economic report due out next week, Economic Planning Agency (EPA) Vice Minister Shimpei Nukaya told a news conference on Friday.

Asked about the monthly economic report to be released next week, Nukaya said views on some factors may change. "But the situation does not call for a change in the overall view in the report," he said.

Most of the major economic indicators for June have already been released, and although there was a negative impact from the consumption tax increase in April, the effect was within expectations, Nukaya said.
"The recovery trend of the economy is continuing," he said.
Despite a bigger-than-expected fall in industrial production data in June, output is generally on a recovery trend, Nukaya said.
The unemployment rate remained at a record high 3.5 percent but job offers had increased slightly, so the job situation was also gradually improving, he said.
But he added that the government needed to keep watch over housing starts, which had fallen fairly drastically in June.
Although the impact of the sales tax rise on household spending was lingering, corporate capital spending remained steady, he said.
